structure:
ruling-interaction-designer-2026-11-09.md: a short Markdown ruling file, 41 lines, holding the interaction designer's answers to the design questions the waiting-on-design rows were blocked on, passed on by Sam the same day (9 November 2026). Laid out in three pieces, in order: a heading and one-line provenance note (lines 1-3, naming the interaction designer as the author, Sam as the route, and the waiting-on-design blocked rows as the question set); a verbatim block quote of the interaction designer's own words (lines 5-21), six question-and-answer pairs each headed by the question's name and increment id — 'Search buttons (inc-188)' answered 'This has been picked up with the snagging list'; 'Region code prefix (inc-190)' answered 'Same above'; 'Amend pop-ups (inc-195)' answered 'These are no longer pop-ups, they are now proper pages which should remove the issue. Designs can be found in 2.1'; 'Templates sort (inc-162)' answered 'Templates has been dropped for now, this unlocks this ticket.'; 'CPH boxes - inc-093' answered 'No need to add the type behaviour on top, it should follow the gov.uk date input behaviour'; and 'Germinal date calendars (inc-192)' answered 'Keep the MOJ date picker.'; then a '## Decided' section (lines 23-41) with exactly six numbered items, one per quoted answer and in the same order, each a bolded headline sentence plus the design question number it answers (questions 1, 2, 9, 11 and 7, and 'the design question for c-283'), the behaviour it settles, the increments it drops or releases (inc-188 and inc-202; inc-190 and inc-204; inc-195 dropped, inc-120, inc-121 and inc-185 building the pages instead; inc-162 and its parked-theme copy inc-248 dropped; inc-093 dropped, inc-219 having built it; inc-192 released from blocked to todo, inc-206 having styled the picker) and a 'Confirms.' or 'New.' marker (items 1 and 2 confirm existing work, items 3 to 6 are new). The scope is 'whole file', so nothing is left out. At 41 lines the file is far smaller than one part, and the extract-ruling method needs the block quote and the numbered reading of it read side by side, so it is one part: the whole file, word for word, with the block quote as the source and the six numbered items as the main session's reading to be checked against it.

Extracted in 1 part:
Part 1, The whole 9 November interaction designer ruling: Part 1 of 1 read the whole of workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-interaction-designer-2026-11-09.md, all 41 lines, and claims every point in it; nothing in the file belongs to another part. The file follows the ruling layout of references/DISTIL.md section 6, in three pieces. (a) Heading and provenance, lines 1-3: '# Ruling: the interaction designer, 9 November 2026' and one sentence, 'Answers to the design questions the waiting-on-design rows were blocked on, passed on by Sam the same day.' — so the author is the interaction designer, the route is Sam, the date is 9 November 2026 and the question set is the design questions the waiting-on-design rows were blocked on. (b) A verbatim block quote of the interaction designer's own words, lines 5-21, six question-and-answer pairs in this order: 'Search buttons (inc-188)' / 'This has been picked up with the snagging list'; 'Region code prefix (inc-190)' / 'Same above'; 'Amend pop-ups (inc-195)' / 'These are no longer pop-ups, they are now proper pages which should remove the issue. Designs can be found in 2.1'; 'Templates sort (inc-162)' / 'Templates has been dropped for now, this unlocks this ticket.'; 'CPH boxes — inc-093' / 'No need to add the type behaviour on top, it should follow the gov.uk date input behaviour'; 'Germinal date calendars (inc-192)' / 'Keep the MOJ date picker.' That block quote is the source. (c) A '## Decided' section, lines 23-41, with exactly six numbered items, one per quoted answer and in the same order: 1 search buttons already done (design question 1, inc-202 built the joined blue search button from the designers' snagging list, inc-188 went with it, nothing changes, 'Confirms.'); 2 region code prefix already done (design question 2, built in design snagging inc-204 which took in inc-190, nothing changes, 'Confirms.'); 3 amend and cancel amendment are pages, not dialogs (design question 9, the Design Release 2.1 designs show them as their own pages, inc-120 and inc-121 in manage-notifications build them, inc-185 builds them for germinal products, inc-195 the dialogs over the page is dropped, 'New.'); 4 no templates sort (design question 11, templates dropped for now which ruling:sam-2026-11-04 had already parked so the sort question is settled by that, inc-162 and its parked-theme copy inc-248 dropped, 'If templates come back, the sort comes back as a question with them', 'New.'); 5 the county parish holding boxes take no JavaScript on top (design question 7, they behave as the GOV.UK date input does — separate labelled boxes, no digit filter, no paste spreading, no focus moving — which design snagging-b inc-219 built, inc-093 dropped, 'New.'); 6 the germinal dates keep the MOJ date picker (the design question for c-283, each germinal date gets the 'Choose date' calendar, the Ministry of Justice date picker every other date in both frontends uses and design snagging inc-206 styled, not replaced by the three-part date input, inc-192 released from blocked to todo, 'New.'). The six numbered items are the main session's reading of the block quote, so each is checked against the quote: the headline decisions are marked verbatim where the quoted words say them (pages not pop-ups, designs in 2.1, templates dropped, no type behaviour on top, follow the gov.uk date input behaviour, keep the MOJ date picker), and everything the quote does not say in so many words is marked inferred with the quoted words that imply it named in the statement or note — every snagging increment id (inc-202, inc-204, inc-219, inc-206), the increments that build the amend and cancel amendment pages (inc-120, inc-121, inc-185), the parked-theme copy inc-248, the cross-reference to ruling:sam-2026-11-04, the four behaviours ruled out on the CPH boxes, the 'Choose date' label, the 'every other date in both frontends' claim, the 'not the three-part date input' exclusion, and every drop, release or 'nothing changes'. Each item's design question number (1, 2, 9, 11, 7) and item 6's conflict c-283 are recorded in the claim notes. Coverage of this part: the provenance sentence, all six quoted answers and all six numbered items are claimed, 48 claims in all, of which six are gap claims naming points the ruling touches and leaves open — the sort question if templates return, where in Design Release 2.1 the amend designs are, what the GOV.UK date input behaviour means for a county parish holding number which is not a date, whether 'Same above' means the same snagging item as the search buttons, which germinal dates the MOJ picker covers, and whether a germinal date still works without JavaScript when the picker is kept. The file carries no tables, images or links to other documents.
